utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge Robinson will be absent for the first session due to urgent -- some personal reasons, so two of us will sit pursuant to 15 bis. Mr. Milosevic, for you to continue your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the past few days, we looked at what your tasks were, and you demonstrated this through your orders and analyses. Yesterday we established that the situation in Kosovo and Metohija grew increasingly more complex. Now we will see what kind of tasks you issued with regard to defence and attack to your motorised brigade in your area of responsibility in the in-depth securing of the state border. This is an order signed by you on the 14th of February, and it's in tab 295. Along with it there is a map, so that I would like you to explain what the tasks were, to show us the map, and to tell us only the most essential points contained in this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't have a map at 295.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have a map either.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: While I'm on my feet and while we're mentioning maps, the witness returned this morning having selected a map to deal with the Ashdown evidence. He's marked it in a way that he's explained to Ms. Dicklich, and therefore he's in a position to deal with this. I don't think the accused had a chance to look at it yet. I'm, of course, entirely in the Court's hands. We could get it copied now or we could wait for it to be used on the overhead projector and then get it copied later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, I think you can deal with it during your cross-examination, but I have to consult with -- yes, I see nodding, so that can be explored during the cross-examination. Mr. Milosevic, do we have a separate map for tab 295?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do have a map, Mr. Kwon, and I can tell you that I was surprised by the fact that things were missing yesterday because a CD was provided with all the documents, so the service here and my documents were taken from the same CD. So what was printed out for me must be available for everyone in the courtroom. It's all on the CD, it can all be found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me find it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's tab 295.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among the maps I was given, I can't find this particular map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I put the map I have on the ELMO. It's black and white.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, General, can you see the map on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let us proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, please read out what it says here on the map. Tell us what this map shows, who approved the map, who signed it, and whether the map says it's an order for defence and attack given to the 549th.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my order accompanying the order for attack and defence. It is an order issued at 1000 hours on the 14th of February, 1999, at the temporary command post. And from this map we can see how the mixed companies are deployed which were allowed under the agreement. And we can see that they were deployed each in its own area. We can also see the disposition of the border posts. And these arrows show the directions of the possible engagement of these mixed companies, indicating also the tasks assigned to them. Although, through the order attached to this decision on the map, all the tasks given to the units are defined with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, the point of my question is in the tasks. Let me explain right away that there is no mystery here. Mr. Nice keeps saying that our forces had tasks other than those mentioned here, that their task was to perpetrate ethnic cleansing, to kill the civilian population, the non-Serb population, that is. He has various kinds of constructions that he has presented here, so I want to see what the order is that you as the brigade commander issued. And there were others in the chain of command, both superior to you and junior to you. What were the tasks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There can be no question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear to every normal person. But look here. What does it say here in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To prevent the infiltration, to "prevent weapons and military equipment being brought in, break up and destroy terrorist groups infiltrated. Use the other forces in cooperation with the MUP to secure control of the territory within the zone of responsibility, and an unhindered flow of traffic on the Prizren-Djakovica axis, step up the security of military facilities --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read a little bit slower. Bear in mind the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "-- and to be prepared to intervene in -- with regard to the sectors or facilities under threat and to break up and destroy sabotage and terrorist forces." I received this task directly from the corps command, and as such it entered my order and could not be changed. And also, my -- the location of my forward command post and command post are mentioned. And then the neighbouring units are assigned tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The map, as I see, was approved by the higher command as part of your order.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraph 4 practically is my own decision. And this is what is shown on the map. The decision says that: "In the zone assigned, by using the main brigade forces, to secure the DG and combat control of the territory and prevent the infiltration of DTS, and with the auxiliary forces protect military facilities, personnel and TMS in the barracks and outlying facilities, with part of the forces at readiness to intervene on axes under threat." The goal of this task -- rather, this decision is to secure the state border in depth. That's one thing. And monitor -- monitoring and combat control of the territory, prevent the transfer of DTS and military equipment to Kosovo and Metohija, break up and destroy infiltrated DTS, protect military facilities, units, and the materiel, and establish conditions for the rapid engagement of other forces. And further, the combat deployment is described.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. What does it say in the last sentence in paragraph 4.7 of your order to the units subordinate to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That "in the execution of all tasks assigned, fully respect the prescribed procedures for dealing with prisoners of war, and the regulations of the Geneva Convention, humanitarian law, and the law of war." That is the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, if you could remind me of what is a DTS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sabotage terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now we are entering the third decade [as interpreted] of February, and in view of the threats issued by the NATO pact we now have here your decision about redeploying materiel and equipment. Can you explain the purpose of your decision and why you arrived at this decision and how it was carried out.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's well known that the equipment and materiel of every army is located in certain depots and warehouses which are concentrated in one place in order to be more easily secured. In a situation where there is an imminent threat of war, these -- the equipment and materiel are dislocated to various locations so that if they are destroyed, they are not all destroyed together and the unit can still have resources left. The purpose of scattering the equipment and materiel is to have it in various locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. This is a clear explanation. Tell me now, as you carried out an analysis, yesterday you said every time there is a movement of troops, after that every commander, including you, carries out an analysis of what has been done and documents the aim and what happened. In tab 297, you have an analysis of what was done on the 29th of February, 1999. What do you say in this analysis?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 29th of February, 1999 -- on the 20th of February, 1999, a group of officers was looking for the right kind of terrain for this kind of redeployment. Metohija Vino is a very well-known company, so they went to that area, and they were attacked by terrorist forces in those vineyards belonging to that company. Since this was a small group of officers with a very small security detail, these combat vehicles were hit and these units -- or rather, officers asked for assistance. This analysis practically shows our intervention -- or rather, the intervention of the forces that came to assist them; that is to say, those who deblocked this group of officers, who chased away the terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's just deal with this so it's quite clear what was actually going on. Because of the imminent threat of a NATO aggression, you were dispersing your materiel resources; ammunition, fuel, equipment, what the brigade had.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A group of officers went out to reconnoiter, to see where all of this would be redeployed. They have no combat tasks. And then they were attacked by terrorists. They call a combat unit to their aid because they're not capable of defending themselves, this unit comes, intervenes, and on the basis of all of that, you make this analysis as to what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is presented through this analysis. As a rule, such things are contained in the verification team of the OSCE, because they were present too. Soon after that, five vehicles of the OSCE from Suva Reka and Prizren arrived in the immediate vicinity of this particular locality. Three vehicles arrived to the side where the terrorists were, those who were attacking, and two vehicles arrived to where my unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you also wrote an analysis on the basis of reconnaissance on the 20th -- on the 21st of February, and you informed the corps command. Can it be seen in this analysis what the actual task of your unit was? That is in tab 298.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, on the basis of orders issued by the superior command on the 21st of February we moved in two directions, Prizren-Suva Reka, Recane, Sopina, Musutiste, Dvorane, and Prizren, Bela Crkva, Orahovac, Zociste, and the other way around. The command is informed that during these activities there were no contacts with terrorist forces and also they are informed of the observations made during the reconnaissance. Near Suva Reka, persons in uniform were noticed, towards Budak [phoen] and Matica [phoen]. When arriving in the village of Vranic, the population was surprised to see the army and they started fleeing towards the mosque, and that shows that possibly there were terrorists hiding in the village itself. In the village of Recane, they noticed the movement of persons in civilian clothes in the area. Then they fled into the bushes. All of this was observed by members of the OSCE and there were also cameramen from Western countries who actually filmed the movement of troops. Near Maleso [phoen], we came to Vran Stena, and that is where we noticed certain persons and we assumed that they were observers. Near Zociste, we noticed that from Samodreza and Studencani the population was moving out on their own vehicles in the direction of Neprebiste and others, and there were only terrorist forces left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Before that, it says here they're intensively working on digging communication trenches and bunkers.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what it says. For the area of Retimlje, they're building trenches, communication trenches, and bunkers intensively. MUP organs that are in Vran Stena noticed during contact with them that the trenches dating back to 1998 were being renewed at the Troja pass and that they were going to Orahovac-Malisevo but only with members of the OSCE and that they practically observed terrorist forces in uniform by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You see, already in document 299, you indicate the information that you gathered over those days about the number of persons who were carrying out tactical training in the area of the village of Pojate.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was characteristic of the entire territory of the Albanian HAS; that is to say, the part of the territory that is on the Albanian side, that there was intensive training in the immediate border area. In the previous order -- in my previous order, there is mention of that, how many terrorist forces are in my zone -- or rather, in Albania neighbouring my zone, ranging between 4.000 to 6.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all of that is going on already in the third week of February.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I'm just going to put a few short questions to you in relation to your relationship with the verification mission during the month of February. The documents that pertain to the verification mission are in numbers 300 to 320 inclusive. In order to save time and since these are documents that provide day-to-day information about contacts between the army and the verification mission and the regular functioning of this relationship, I don't think I have to deal with all the documents individually one by one, but I'm simply asking you to give us your briefest possible comment about these documents, 300 to 320, that all pertain to the month of February and the verification mission.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all can I say something in relation to myself. In tab Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 301 on the 1st of February, I met up with the leader of area one, General Maisonneuve, and he told me that he had 160 verifiers and 160 assistants. There are three centres and three -- in Slapusevo, Malisevo, and Rastane, and that he was -- and that he intended to open three other centres in Zupa, Planeja, and Velika Krusa. I gave some proposals then that in some other places these sub-centres should be open too, and the general accepted that. However, that did not happen, because everything that happened in the month of March prevented that from happening. In tab 301 also, the representatives of the OSCE highlight that only the Siptars were asking them for help, and the impression therefore was that they were the only ones who were jeopardised, not the Serbs. In all the tabs from 300 to 320 the first thing mentioned is that our side informs the mission on a daily basis about troop movement and about military convoy movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, is this the pattern how the relationship functioned with the mission? Can we take any one of these reports? Again, is paragraph 1 always troop movement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, we are on tab 301. If the general could explain in more detail how this report is written, written by whom, in what context. And I note it's written by team leader Major General Tomislav Mladenovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In all units, in all independent battalions -- that is to say, there are three battalions that were within the Pristina Corps -- and in every brigade there were liaison officers. Liaison officers sent daily reports to the liaison team of the Pristina Corps. And also, there was the liaison team of the 3rd Army that was in Pristina too. The liaison team of the 3rd Army on a daily basis, when they received reports from the ground, from the field, they would send their own reports to the General Staff, and that's the kind of report you have before you now. This is practically from the entire territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Everything that happened and that had to do with the OSCE mission was forwarded to the operative centre of the General Staff in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So all these tabs are of the same category, so written by a report of the 3rd Army command mission liaison team.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Yes. These are top-level reports that reached Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One housekeeping matter: Tab 300, the index says: "A translation is provided," but in my binder, translation is missing. Just -- is it just my case? That can be sorted out. Yes. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, while we are still dealing with tab 301 that Mr. Kwon devoted particular attention to, can we see a pattern here according to which these reports are written? Actually, is paragraph 1 always movements by units? Does the movement of every unit have to be recorded and submitted to the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is in accordance with the agreement from the level of company further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Any kind of movement, whether they're coming or going, that is always paragraph 1, and in paragraph 1 any movement of any troops is referred to.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Number 2: "Incidents."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incidents that are caused by terrorists, or, for example, incidents that involved the OSCE mission, that were directed against the OSCE mission. So it has to do with everything that happened in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And number 3 is observations on activity by the OSCE mission and its members.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Contacts of the mission, meetings, and everything else that the mission did vis-a-vis the units where liaison officers had contacts; that is to say, this team was informed of all these contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it always says who led the team of the OSCE, who they talked to, at which particular localities, where they were, and so on and so forth. So the entire activity is invariably registered. Is that the pattern that was used?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even the vehicles, the OSCE vehicles, and the persons who were present, except in some cases when the persons present did not want to introduce themselves, but most often there is reference to the name and surname of the persons involved, the countries they came from, and the role they play in the mission itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Is that roughly how information was provided each and every time and the length of the text depends on what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any incidents in the relations between the army and the mission in any respect? Was any such thing referred to in any one of these tabs?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in these 20 tabs. I just wish to point out that in tab 303, this was characteristic for my zone. There was a group of villages, Dobruste, Vrbnica, especially Dobruste, which is in the border area. Every day the mission was invited to come and visit these villages, and every day they sought approval for that and toured the villages, allegedly because the population was under threat. Also, on the 7th of February the locals denied what the mission claimed, that they were moving out because the army was opening fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where are you reading this from?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 303.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What page? At the end.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The liaison officer visited Dobruste with the OSCE representatives who talked to the villagers. The villagers denied the mission's claim that they were moving out because VJ units opened fire at night. So the mission is telling you that they're moving out because the army opens fire at night, and then you go to the village together with the mission to establish what was actually going on in actual fact. And then they denied what the mission claimed. Did they tell you where they got this information from?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were reports that they received by telephone. The same is contained in tab 308, dated the 12th of February. But this was a bigger meeting with villagers from that particular village again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Somebody was very diligent in submitting these false reports, somebody from that village was. Now, tell me, where is this in tab 308? Yes, paragraph 3, "Observations, talks with the villagers on freedom of movement because they submitted a report to humanitarian organisations stating that they were prohibited from doing so."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last paragraph in 308: "The mission -- the mission team," rather --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the English translation hasn't been provided for this tab, contrary to the indication in the index.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, Mr. Kwon. All the materials for General Delic were submitted here on the 20th of April. Today is June 30th. So 70 days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So when we don't have an English translation, and if you're going to deal with it in detail, why don't you put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, just have a look at this page. It's on the second page, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at that page. We won't have a look at the entire report. Read it through. And we'd like to be able to follow it on the overhead projector, but do read out what you wanted to quote.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of February, between 9.00 and 11.30 hours, a meeting was held between representatives of the OSCE, the liaison officers, and something in the village of Dobruste -- and the inhabitants of the village of Dobruste. It says in the course of the day a meeting was held with representatives from the village, a village in which they stated that they didn't have any problems with members of the Army of Yugoslavia. And the OSCE members said that they were happy to see children freely going to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The liaison officer asked senior inhabitants of the village why inhabitants were moving out. He asked how many families had left the village up until then and how many families there were working and abroad. He also wanted to know which countries they were working in. The answer was that the inhabitants were afraid of army patrols. To date, ten families had moved out and there were about a hundred families in the village who were living abroad -- or a hundred families from the village living abroad, mostly in Slovenia. Most of them had gone to Slovenia, they had moved to Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they, the inhabitants, wanted to have more frequent contact with the command of the unit who was in their immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And these 20 documents, which include reports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that not a different explanation? The villagers are on this occasion saying that army patrols are what has caused them to move out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's something that they said, because on that day -- or rather, during that period of time, in the vicinity of their village a warehouse full of weapons and ammunition was found in a cave near a lake. If you have a look at the map, I will point to the location of that village. The village of Dobruste is here, next to the village. In the immediate vicinity of the village, in two places, large quantities of weapons and ammunition were found. These weapons and ammunition were checked by the OSCE too. On that day, until they had verified this, until they had checked this, throughout the night army patrols remained there and guarded the place where weapons and ammunition had been found. And in another report, you will be able to see that members of the mission told these villagers that they personally saw when fire was opened on the army from their village, and not a single army in the world would have tolerated such things. They said that it was necessary to put an end to such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: First of all, the first of these tabs you referred to, 303, the villagers denied the mission's claim that they had been abused by the army or that the army was in any way acting against their interest. But now on 308 we have the villagers themselves saying that people have moved out, not just are moving out today, but have moved out because of their fear of army patrols. They've emigrated from the area and gone to other places. Now, these two don't -- these are inconsistent with each other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These two things are inconsistent because these reports were made on two different days. There are other reports, and we will deal with them later, we'll see them later, in which the villagers yet again state that they had no problems, because in this village the OSCE mission was present every two or three days, and they asked for permission to visit the village on such occasions. It's true that they stated what you can see in the document, but when we have a look at one of the following documents, I will draw your attention to some other facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But while dealing with this section, General, at the beginning of the paragraph, it says that a meeting was held between representatives of the OSCE and the liaison officer. They went to visit the village of Dobruste, and this was made possible for them.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And in the same paragraph, it says that there was a meeting with village representatives and at that meeting they stated that they had no problems with army members and the mission representatives said that they were happy because they could see children freely going to school. And then there is the part which states that they were afraid of patrols. So at the same meeting they said that they had no problems with the army, children were going to school, but at the same time they were afraid of patrols.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have a look at this map, you can see where this unit was deployed. It's in the immediate vicinity of the village in question. Sometimes at night fire was opened, because this unit had been attacked from this feature, the Brinje [phoen] feature, which is here, and the inhabitants heard the shooting for sure, and they had good reason to be afraid because they were in the immediate vicinity of the border area and the troops were in their vicinity. When they said they had no problems with the army, that meant they had no problems because the army wasn't causing them any problems. But as for the fact that they were afraid, well, that's a totally individual matter. And the fact that they felt at threat, well, other people would have probably felt at threat too, other people of different ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the border area, there was sporadic fire at that time too.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Are there any other examples that you could provide, examples that you have been referring to? Perhaps we could concentrate on just a few of these documents.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning of March there is an example I could provide. Under tab 310, it says "The village of Planeja was visited, which is also located in the border area, and humanitarian aid for the school had been promised. The director said that they had no problems --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and therefore the speed at which the witness is going may be inconvenient for the interpreters but it's actually quite hard for comprehension. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We don't have an English translation. Could you put it on the ELMO. I'm concerned about the way you're presenting the -- your evidence. Your index clearly says that translations have been provided, but it's not. Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here at the very beginning, it has the date of the 15th of December [as interpreted]. There was a report from the inhabitants according to which there was shooting in the village. This was in the village of Zulfaj, the village of Zulfaj is located here, and it's in the border area too, in the immediate vicinity of the border with Albania.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, in the transcript it says the 15th of December; whereas, the witness said the 15th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The date was the 15th of February, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The mission concluded that the inhabitants weren't living in the village permanently, they were living in Djakovica and they only came to the village to feed the livestock. OSCE representatives checked the houses and noted that no damage had been inflicted on the houses as a result of shooting. The shooting that could be heard was a result of an incident that occurred in Karaula one week earlier when an illegal group of terrorists tried to cross the state border illegally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You're now explaining what happened. But here it says there was no damage inflicted on the houses which was a result of alleged shooting. The shooting was in the Karaula-Vodin [phoen] area seven days ago, and this could be heard in the village mentioned. That's what it says in the report.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says the mission representative expressed his satisfaction because there was training that was organised and there were no incidents.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in a different area. Units of the army were involved in training and mission representatives monitored the training. This is a company from the 125th Brigade in the Vucikan [phoen] sector and they were accompanied by a mission team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all these activities were monitored, each and every movement, any form of training was monitored. In any of these other documents, do you have reports on visits to certain villages?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The other documents refer to meetings held at various levels, meetings between local teams and liaison officers, and at higher levels, meetings in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General Delic, do any of these reports include any references to complaints by the OSCE -- complaints by the OSCE of aggressive conduct by VJ forces or complaints recorded by villagers of aggressive conduct by VJ forces, or do all the reports give the VJ a clean bill of health?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can also find examples of such reports in the report in March. There was information on incidents that the mission reported on with regard to their members. And with respect to what we are discussing, these village visits, this is all a result of reports submitted to certain mission teams in which it was stated that there had been certain incidents or in which it was stated that the army had posed a threat to the inhabitants. In the vast majority of these reports, as you can see, the mission established quite -- something that was completely different in the field, came to a completely different conclusion in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you point to an example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in this month, I have a report from March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you have at hand?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 1st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which tab is that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you now. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's tab 4 -- it's tab 448. And that can be found in binder 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We haven't received yet tab 400-something. We can come back to that issue, and let's -- let us proceed for the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll deal with that in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So can we ignore the other documents up to tab 320, documents which include information on the work of the mission. Is it necessary for you to make any other comments with regard to some of these documents?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I'll comment on one other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it is for you to single out the important events, not for the witness. But let's proceed this time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 317. Tab 317, and it's page 3, the third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could indicate the paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What are you referring to? Could you read it out?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the course of the day, OSCE representatives in Pec were trying to persuade their assistants and interpreter to leave the territory of Kosovo and Metohija together with them." So it's page 3, and I have mentioned the tab number already, 317.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you can see that the mission is preparing to leave Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's on the 19th of February. On the same day in Pristina a meeting was held of representatives of the OSCE at the request of General Drewienkiewicz, attended by Mr. Loncar and other team leaders. The subject of discussion was increased army activity and offering assistance to evacuate the OSCE mission. And I wanted to emphasise the fact that Mr. Drewienkiewicz said that he had information that members of MUP were preparing operations against the OSCE mission dressed up in KLA uniforms and were planning an assassination attempt on Walker. And this has nothing to do with anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So our police provided security for the mission throughout that period of time. Do you know whether a single member of the mission came to any harm?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only two members of the verification mission were wounded. I think they were from Scotland. But this was in the Decani area and they were wounded by terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Here Drewienkiewicz is telling you that the MUP will open fire on the mission when withdrawing, dressed up in KLA uniforms. The MUP escorted the mission up to the border to ensure they could leave in safety. Are you aware of the fact?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of the fact that is referred to in the March reports. Ambassador Walker thanked MUP members at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: For having escorted him, for not having shot him, and for not having attacked him. That's what he said, and Drewienkiewicz. In any event, we've seen what Drewienkiewicz has had to say and in the film we saw that he was not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bonomy, Judge Bonomy put a question with regard to the incidents. On page 7 --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's not to be allowed. Comments like that are simply not allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you should not comment like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you will give the same warning to Mr. Nice when he puts forth his comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to understand the different functions of an advocate, which he attempts to be now, and counsel who is entitled and indeed obliged to put the nature of his case to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like the parties to proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will proceed, Mr. Kwon, but that side should not falsify the facts and not obstruct the proceedings intentionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please proceed when you're told to proceed by the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't get excited, Mr. Bonomy. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, General, what is noted down here about the incidents you wanted to talk about -- you mentioned, as far as I can recall, page 7.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tab 317, page 7. This is what the mission stated at the meeting about overstepping authority by the army in relation to members of the mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to quote the passage.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pointing weapons towards the vehicles of the verifiers escorting a unit on the march, 13 times. Stopping verifiers at gunpoint and removing them from camp areas, twice. Unnecessary use of force, once. Ban on verifiers passing through unit deployment areas, ten times. Searches and confiscation of items, twice. And verbal threats, once."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Are these major incidents? Did anything happen to anyone?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, there were frequent attempts to enter the border area or even the camp premises where the verifiers tried to lift the barrier and tried to enter. And the men manning the barrier acted according to the rules of the service, to prevent such illegal actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It says here on page 8: "In all cases, when they arrived unannounced and without the liaison officer, members of the mission were not allowed access to the unit."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was this in compliance with the rules that they should arrive together with the liaison officer?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these were camp premises and this was the border area, and this was constantly a topic of negotiations. And finally, in late March it was agreed that the teams should not come to the border area without a liaison officer. When they arrived in the company of a liaison officer, there were never any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did this have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you direct me to that passage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 8. It's on page 8, the third paragraph, where it says: "In all cases, when they arrived unannounced and without a liaison officer, the members of the mission were not allowed access and passage through the area of deployment of the units."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In English, page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, were there practical reasons for this?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a liaison officer is present, then the army takes responsibility for the safety of the members of the mission from the time they leave the garrison throughout the time of their stay. The liaison officer is the person who is familiar with the territory, the roads, the communications. And the practical reasons are that when a liaison officer turns up together with the members of the mission, this means that the superior commander knows that the mission is in the area and that the superior -- or rather, the officer on the ground doesn't have to worry about having to call his commander and inform him that a vehicle has arrived and he doesn't have to ask whether he's allowed to let it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So everything is resolved when they follow the envisioned procedure.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So when they followed the procedure prescribed, everything was all right. But when they didn't, they were not allowed access.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's quite clear, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, could you read the passage contained in the last paragraph under the heading (h). Could you read that passage, the 24th of February.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "On the 24th of February, in the Donja Brnjica village sector, a member of the 52nd Battalion of the ABHO approached a member of the OSCE Mission who had come to the unit's deployment area and said: 'We'll kill you, you animals! This is Serbia.'" This is the threat I mentioned, one verbal threat. This is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to this soldier who made this verbal threat afterwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As this was not a unit of mine, I am not aware of it. But when the members of the mission listed all these incidents, they were told that everything would be checked. Whenever the mission presented, not only in relation to the mission itself but also in relation to the civilian population, whenever they presented any problems, all officers were duty-bound to check their allegations within their change of command and to take the appropriate steps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And these reports were sent to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am telling you. You can see on every page that the report was received by the operations centre of the General Staff. There is a stamp on the last page showing that it was received by the operations centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And reports would be sent to the political leaders by the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These reports became part of an operative report. They did not leave the General Staff, but the events, the most important events from these reports, would be included in the operative report of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Go on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me clarify. Mr. Kwon, you can see on this example before you now to whom this was addressed, "To: The General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia - to the team for liaison with the OSCE and NATO." So that was the part of the General Staff that would receive this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: These documents now ending with number 320, relating to the work of the verification mission, is now something we can lay aside. I hope, General, that there is nothing left in dispute here. General, the command of the Pristina Corps -- and I can see that it says "deputy commander" here, the person acting for the commander, Colonel Veroljub Zivkovic, on the 7th of March sent to the command of the 549th Brigade, to the commander personally, or the Chief of Staff, that is to you or your Chief of Staff, this dispatch. What -- this is tab 321, General. And what is contained in it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a telegram, a dispatch from the commander of the Pristina Corps, sent after my telegram where I reported that in the area of the village of Jeskovo terrorist forces were reassembling. This is a telegram saying that by 1400 hours on the 8th of March I should deliver to the corps command my plan for destroying this group and the composition of the forces I would deploy, and also I was to call on part of the MUP forces to participate in this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. I will now put a few questions to you in view of the testimony of a protected witness here, A43, in connection with this incident. What, General, was the essence of the plan to destroy the terrorist forces in the broader area of the village of Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this follows from what we can see from the documents that will follow. So the main idea was that around Prizren groups of terrorists numbering 20 to 30 men began to appear, and they were mobilising the population and re-taking the territory, as had happened in 1998. Their aim was to block the town of Prizren and to cut off the communications leading from Prizren into the depth of the state territory, also to cut off the logistical supply routes. I reported on this to the corps command and requested approval to neutralise these terrorist forces and disarm them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is your request contained in tab 322, where you write to the command of the Pristina Corps, and this contains your plan for the breaking up and destruction of terrorist forces in the broader area of the village of Jeskovo, south of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This tab is a response to the telegram from tab 321, where I was asked to deliver my plan. Here I'm sending my plan after consulting the chief of the secretariat of the MUP as to what forces and units would be engaged and how the operation against the terrorist forces was to be carried out. This is my proposal to the command, and here I also propose the time of the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we move on, the -- the accused's reference to protected witness A43 is clearly an error. And rather than leave that error to confuse later readers of the transcript, we better get the correct identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: K41, I think, is the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And perhaps Mr. Milosevic can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: According to the LiveNote, it would appear to be probably K31 -- K41. It may be K42, but I think it's K41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. In my notes, it says K43, but this may be an error. In any case, there was a witness called by Mr. Nice who testified here and whose testimony described a completely different situation from the one described by General Delic, but General Delic's forces were there and he knows exactly what happened. So that there will be no problem, it will be easy to establish the truth and discredit yet another witness as completely false.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. If the witness is K40-something, that's -- we have only K41. It should be K41. Could you check it during the break and confirm it after the -- after the break, please. And in the meantime, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's see what happened with your proposal and your plan for the breaking-up and destruction. Tab 323 is an order issued by the command of the Pristina Corps approving my proposal for the deployment of the troops, and the order states that I should proceed to destroy the Siptar forces according to my proposal of the 11th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So your idea is accepted here.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then is this the entire technical procedure: You report, they ask for a plan, they accept your plan. After that you issue an order about the engagement of the forces. Is this the order contained in tab 324?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are two ways of proceeding: If the superior command issues a direct order for the carrying-out of a task, then only a decision, an order, and an analysis or report are drawn up. If I, as you will remember from the order of 1998, for example, which said that units were not to be engaged without an order from the command. So I had to report on the appearance of terrorist forces, and I had to propose to the command what should be done. Then the corps command asks me for a plan, how I envision the carrying-out of this task. They can either approve my plan or change it. In this case, my plan was approved. So the corps command ordered me to carry out my plan. I issued the decision then, which is shown on the map, and I also issued an order to my units. It's contained in tab 324.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's the order that I'm asking you about precisely; that is to say, the order that you issued to your units that is contained in tab 324. Can you comment on it very briefly?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that "During the night between the 3rd and the 4th of March in the village of Jeskovo a terrorist group was infiltrated consisting of 25 terrorists, and immediately the following night the villages of Leskovac, Ljubicevo, Hoca Zagradska were toured with the aim of mobilising the Siptar population." Further on there is reference to the 5th and 6th and the activities then, that this group was joined by a large of group of some 50 terrorists from Retimlje, that on that day a diversionary attack was launched on the mixed company that was here near the lake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... did you give to your forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That can be seen through the tasks given to the units. That is paragraph 5. "Unit tasks, 5/1, 5/2, 5/3, 5/4, 5/5 and 5/6. Precisely every unit gets its own tasks. First the composition of the unit, where they will be moving from, where the lines of blockade are, what tasks they have during the actual operations, and if you wish, I can read out any one of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, this is a very detailed precise order that you issued that contains all elements envisaged for such orders. Is there a map attached, as customary along with such orders?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The map is in tab 325. This is a map where it says "Decision of the commander of the motorised brigade to destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the wider area of Leskovo," approved by Major Lazarevic and signed by Brigade Commander Bozidar Delic. And the entire situation is depicted here on the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Red denotes the army forces that were engaged. Blue denotes the area where the terrorist forces are. Green denotes the deployment of MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, in paragraph, for example, 5.6 and some -- 5.4, I noticed there a mention of PJP. Are they members of special police? "37 Od PJP."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So police were operating together under the control of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you elaborate further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You misspoke. They did not operate under my control. This was joint activity of the army and the MUP. Special units of the police -- well, I'm not a police expert, but it's not a special police force as such. It is part of the regular police force, consisting of younger men who are, say, better trained and equipped than the other police. They did not have the status of any kind of special police as such. I think that General Stevanovic must have explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He explained that, but the translation that is used here is always "special police." They probably cannot find a different word.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They belonged to the regular police force but they are younger persons who went through some military training partially, and they are more capable than other members of the police force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, if you could give us a -- some general picture, a description of a general picture how a joint operation with the police is taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In preparation, before this kind of map is drawn and before an order is written, it's obvious that it was me -- or rather, that my organs drew this map and that they wrote the order. That is only natural, because the army is particularly trained for that and they have organs that deal with map-drawing as such. The commander of the MUP unit is there to coordinate things together with me; that is to say, the operations of his unit, because his unit has less combat capacity. It does not have proper support. As a rule, they have small arms only. So viewing the terrain where the action will be carried out, they -- we decide where the police will be engaged. In order to coordinate command in this particular case and practically in all cases when we operated together with the police, the commander of this unit would be right next to me. We would be together. He would command his troops; I would command my troops. Of course, we give each other assistance. If he needs medical support or any kind of support, of course I will help out. Also, if I need assistance, I will get that assistance from the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who decides, first of all, that there should be a joint operation of military and the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, in the preceding tab, that is, tab 323 -- let me just have a look. You -- or rather, 321, tab 321, the last paragraph. The corps command says after my report, when I submit my idea how this will be done and how the forces would be grouped, and that I include in preparing the action part of the MUP forces. So the corps command says that before I actually elaborate the idea, I get in touch with the chief of the secretariat also on my territory and in that territory of mine he is responsible for that part of the zone, that we plan this activity together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Over all can I take it that in the end the police is subordinated to the -- to the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No way. No way. That cannot be inferred at all. The two systems are fully equal. As far as 1998 is concerned, the police was the proponent of activities against terrorism and the army was there to support the police. The situation was similar in the beginning of 1999. Specifically in this particular action, we can see according to the forces engaged that it was the army that was the mainstay and that it was the police that was acting in concert with them, but there was no need for me to command all these forces. In order to avoid certain problems, I and the commander - if you look at the map here, you will see where my command post is. You will see this flag, and that denotes my command post - I and the commander of the MUP unit are together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is not clear from the map. Could you -- about putting that part on the -- on the ELMO and -- if the usher could do that. Fold the map and put it on the ELMO and let the witness point to that point. So it is your claim that we can see the command post -- the command post of MUP chief here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only my command post can be seen here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then there's no -- there's no point in putting on the ELMO then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I -- General, if you look at the document we've got, 324, and if you look at paragraph 5.6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is -- what is that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 326?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "The 37th Detachment of the special police units with a 30/2 PAT move from the barracks along the Kasarna-Dusanov Grad-Cviljen axis and take the --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I want you to give me a -- a definition or a description of what is that particular paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is obvious that two MUP units were engaged. That can be seen from 5.6 and 5.7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But each of these is an order, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And each is an order to a MUP unit. Is that right or -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an order issued to both MUP units. One is the company of the special police unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who gave the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be seen that I signed the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's time to adjourn. We'll break for 20 minutes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you are to continue with your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We broke off, General, when you were answering the question that was put by Mr. Bonomy about the participation of the army and the police in this activity pertaining to the terrorist group in the village of Jeskovo. You explained that from a police point of view this area was under the secretariat of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the secretariat of Prizren is a police colonel; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he had the same rank as you did in the army.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you agree with him on joint activity, or did you receive this from someone else?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with him in the presence of his own commanders. These are the commanders who are under his command, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. On the basis of this agreement, when you make a plan for your overall activity, do you include the activity of his units that take part in the said activity?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was practice at corps level and brigade level during 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the order, on page 5, you can see who it was submitted to. My order was submitted only to my units, not to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But your units should know where the MUP units are.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's only natural. In order to avoid what is called friendly fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So was it for those purposes that this was included, everything that has to do with the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is acting in direct concert, a unit of the MUP and a unit of the army, both of which are state organs, and it is only natural for them to closely cooperate and act in concert.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Through the kindness of the liaison officer, I received what Mr. Nice has in his box. You were right, Mr. Kwon, the witness is K41. "K41 (Prizren-Orahovac-Suva Reka)" and then there is mention of Jeskovo, 700 soldiers -- "[In English] [Previous translation continues] ... together with police special units. Tanks and anti-aircraft guns opened fire on a village and witness and others set out to clean up village, meaning to kill anyone there as were told that it was just KLA members. Witness saw ten dead but no one in KLA uniform. He believes total of 30 were killed. Witness did not see any return fire." [Interpretation] And then it says: "[In English] He received orders from Captain Gavrilovic, commander of logistic battalion, went south of Trnje with 80 to 100 soldiers accompanied by one policeman." [Interpretation] Then it says that they killed some civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that, that is to say, what Mr. Nice's witness said, what can be seen from this operation of yours and what actually did happen?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the next tab too, which is an analysis -- or rather, a report submitted to the superior command. That is tab 326.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the map in tab 325, you explained the deployment of the units and everything you did. 326 is an analysis of what happened. General, I am endeavouring that you give an explanation in view of what this witness had said. So let's see what your analysis says and what did happen in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the analysis, we can see the strength, deployment, and organisation of the Siptar terrorist forces. That's in paragraph 1. It says: "The Siptar terrorist forces offered no resistance in the villages of Les, Ljubicevo, Bilusa, Posliste, and Hoca Zagradska. When they saw the MUP and VJ forces, the inhabitants of these villages were agitated, but they set off in a column towards Leskovac village and Prizren. We stopped and searched them and handed over suspicious people (nine persons) to the MUP organs. We held the rest of the villagers up for a while, until the operations in Jeskovo village were over, and then sent them back home. "The STS offered resistance in Jeskovo village. We estimate that the strength of the STS in the village was between 25 and 30 men. Their defence during the day consisted mainly of direct protection of the STS command in the village. The captured documents indicate that they had three guard posts at which they rotated guards every two hours," and so on and so forth. "There were no special defence positions but had been using the existing buildings since September last year. Some houses in the village had been adapted to accommodate troops and enable preparation of meals."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Milosevic, so it would be better if you directed the witness to a particular passage.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I am directing him to the paragraph he's just read out, since Witness K41 said that there were civilians there, and here at the end of this paragraph it says that in the village itself there were no civilians but only Siptar terrorist forces. They offered resistance and opened fire from small arms and also used hand-held rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You can see from the context that what is at stake is a hand-held rocket launcher. And then it says that "The STS tried to penetrate in the direction of Jeskovo-Hoca Zagradska. From the village of Jeskovo, they tried to obtain the Brutska Glava feature, trig point 1206. Given the fact they were encircled, this attempt to break through failed." Then you mention your estimate of losses, "nine killed, no one was captured. We seized: One POLO Armbrust, one bazooka, two light machine-guns, one 60-millimetre mortar with 16 60-millimetre shells of Chinese make, automatic rifles, and one M-48 millimetre rifle." So you are claiming that there were no civilians in this document, contrary to what the witness stated, who testified that civilians were casualties in the village of Jeskovo.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the village of Jeskovo there was not a single civilian who was a victim. All the individuals were in KLA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The witness says these victims weren't in KLA uniforms; he says they were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The OSCE mission representatives monitored the event. There were three teams in the Hoca Zagradska village. On the following day, since night had fallen, it wasn't possible for them to carry out their verification mission, so they waited for the following day and then with members of the police they went on their verification mission. And as far as I can remember, they found seven KLA members who had been killed. Since there were two others in a different place in the village, there were a total of nine of them. They verified this, and there is a book from the fund for humanitarian law, "As Seen, As Told." They refer to the OSCE mission and to their observations in this territory. And on page 332, reference is made to the fact that the mission were afraid of the possibility of the terrorists becoming organised in that village again. They monitored the event and carried out the verification referred to. There is another book written by the commander of the 2nd Battalion of the KLA 125th Brigade. His name is Rrustem Berisha, and it is called "The Path of Freedom." That is the title of the book. On page 99 of that book, he provides the names of nine KLA members who had been killed. He lists their names. So on that occasion, we could not determine the names of the men killed. He says that they were members of a special unit from the 125th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, could you just clarify for me: In relation to this incident, you personally led your troops into the village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was personally present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. That means that in the OSCE documents, as well as in the documents of the KLA commander, reference is made to terrorist forces and not to civilians.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, without a doubt. The command of the 2nd Battalion of the 125th Brigade referred to the heroic death of nine members of the special unit. That referred on the 11th. And as he says in his book, they were engaged in close combat at a distance of 15 to 20 metres from their enemy and they died a heroic death in the village of Jeskovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So this means that, according to all the information that you had available - and you were present at the scene - a KLA special unit was concerned. None of what the Witness K41 said with regard to the civilians and with regard to the fact that fire was not returned, none of what he said is correct.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is quite absurd to make such a statement. That soldier, Witness K41, was a soldier of mine, employed in the Quartermaster Service. And the reason for which he testified in this way is quite different, but what he said is completely false. This can be confirmed by each and every member of my unit, by each and every officer from my unit who was present there. In the unit that this soldier was a member of -- well, that unit did not participate in that combat and was not present at the scene of the fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you were present at the scene of combat. And what you have just said is something that you yourself personally witnessed.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have already said, at the beginning of the fight and from 4.00 in the morning I was located here. The terrorist forces had selected the village of Jeskovo because it is in mountainous terrain and it is surrounded by very high rocks on all sides. It is very difficult to gain access to that location. So when there was ongoing combat, I descended directly to the village. Withdrawal was attempted via this stream, and I saw weapons and all those terrorists there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, was that the only operation which the army carried out in Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the previous year, 1998, in September --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... there weren't any operations in -- earlier in 1999?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, there weren't. That was the first operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A minute ago when I quoted from the summary provided in the box, it says: "The 2nd, 1999, Jeskovo, 700 soldiers." How many soldiers did you engage for the blockade of the village?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's all stated here in the report. It says that 611 men had been engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I believe that we can move on now. Before we do move on, have a look at the report under tab 326. It says: "From 0830 hours until the end of combat, three OSCE vehicles were located in the village of Hoca Zagradska."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Action came to an end just before night fell. Prior to that point in time, mission members insisted on entering the village while combat was still ongoing, since we were responsible for their security. The officer who was in the Hoca Zagradska sector then suggested that the team leader sign a register so that the army wouldn't be held responsible if they were killed, having entered the area of combat. And then they finally said that they did not want to enter that area before it was safe. And on the following day, they carried out their verification together with MUP forces, and on that occasion I was not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. We can now move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Delic, in this report, I see that the terrorist group, as you put it, consist of 25 or 3 men -- 25 and 30 men. Sorry, between 25 and 30. But your force is -- is of total strength of 600 and more and also included six tanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you not think it's too much, disproportionate? What is your observation on this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely not. You have to be familiar with the tactics employed when fighting terrorist forces. Such strong forces weren't necessary to fight 25 or 30 men, but it was necessary to block the entire sector, since we had information according to which there were forces in Bjeskovo [phoen], in the village of Dubicevo [phoen], in the village of Tustendivo [phoen], and in these other villages, Bilesa [phoen], Hoca Zagradska, Leskovac. We had no information about these villages and it was necessary to have this number of men in order to block this vast sector. It's not possible to block such a sector with fewer men. It was necessary to take the lines and to engage in this blockade. But a far smaller unit was engaged in direct combat with these forces, and in these inhabited places a MUP unit was primarily engaged and three of their members were wounded. And later on, when the terrorists attempted to withdraw via the stream, as we say, they were killed in that area because they had to confront forces the strength of one detachment deployed at that position. A detachment consists of up to about ten men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could explain to me why you needed six tanks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The tanks were usually used for direct fire. As you can see here, they arrived from the Prizren sector. They reached the Hoca Zagradska sector. The village of Jeskovo is here. And they were not directly involved there and they didn't approach this village. They were needed in case it was necessary to fire directly on certain targets.
