According to the information we had, there was no civilian population there and it was possible to open fire on firing positions without this causing any problems because only the terrorists would be at threat and no one else. And in Afghanistan now Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Americans are using 15-tonne bombs to target a terrorist group consisting of several men, and they're also using strategic -- they're also using the Air Force in a strategic manner. It's possible to use such means against terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Maybe I have misunderstood this, but does the report -- is it reasonable to draw the conclusion from the report that the majority of terrorists escaped, in spite of the 600-plus force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. According to our estimates, there were between 25 and 30 of them. That's the information we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... nine -- you killed nine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found notebooks with lists as well, and probably when we imposed the blockade, the remainder, 25 or 30 men, were located here, somewhere in the area of the village of Zur or in some of the other villages where mobilisation was carried out -- or rather, where men were summoned to come to Jeskovo to be trained. We expected to find more of them there, at least 25 to 30 of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's either my arithmetic that's a problem or I'm not reading the same report as you are. But the report says that you estimated the strength of the terrorists in -- in this village as between 25 and 30. Nine were killed, none were captured. Does it not follow that the majority escaped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you've read that correctly. There was an estimate. You know what an "estimate" means, an estimate of their strength. We also found a notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you want to change that estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't want to change it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to change it in any way, because an estimate is made prior to carrying out the task on the basis of the information available. The estimate was that there were 25 to 30 of them. We only managed to find nine of them. So all one can say is that our estimate -- well, we did find a notebook containing 30 names. So at that point in time, when we imposed the blockade, all we can say is that they were not located in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Following your inquiries afterwards to write this, which is an analysis, I understand, of the situation, an analysis after the event, how many terrorists do you now say were in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were nine of them, as it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you killed them all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They all died in the course of combat. They weren't killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I didn't mean to suggest anything other than that they died in combat, but I have to say I find it very difficult to deduce from this report, this analysis, that there were only nine of them there. But thank you for clarifying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, on completion of this action, was a single killed civilian found?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no civilians there at all. The civilians from the villages of Bilusa [phoen] and Hoca Zagradska who had set out in the direction of Prizren were returned to their villages, and that was the end of this entire activity. There were no civilians killed, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. On the 7th of March, 1999 you issued a document concerning the taking of measures of combat security, and this was in the area of deployment of the mixed company number 1. What was this about, General? It's in tab 327.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a warning that I sent to the commander of combat group 1/1 in the area of Planeja, which is in the immediate vicinity of the state border, because on the 7th of March there had been Siptar activity in his area so I warned him that he could have the following goals: To provoke --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That they, rather, have the following goals, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To provoke the Yugoslav Army; to check how vigilant the guards are; and thirdly, to create distraction and divert attention from the incursion in order for the Siptar terrorist forces to cross over the border in another part of the territory. So in view of the above, I asked him to undertake the following measures: To increase vigilance, to have intervention units on standby, to prepare fire to target the areas of possible activities, and to take due care to protect materiel, technical equipment, and troops, and lastly, to report to my command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 9th there is another warning which differs in some elements, and it concerns the taking of additional security measures. This is number 328.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As incidents occurred on a daily basis, not only in my unit but in other units as well, a warning arrived from the command of the Pristina Corps dated the 9th of March from which you can see that throughout Kosovo anti-tank mines were being used on a large scale, as well as improvised mine barriers on the roads, especially those leading to the defence positions of the terrorist forces. And it says here that in the area of Stubla anti-tank mines were laid, several members of the MUP were killed and several seriously wounded, and that in the area of Djeneral Jankovic a reconnaissance vehicle on the 29th was wounded and that two soldiers were seriously injured. To prevent such occurrences, I warned all units and commands to undertake additional security measures, emphasising the assessment of envisaged routes and roads before venturing out and to examine the roads with mine detectors and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that throughout Kosovo and Metohija mines had been laid on which -- which anyone could come across who was not a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 329, you again have a warning, referring to information on large Siptar forces on the territory of the Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that they intended to pass over -- onto our territory in the period between the 13th and 15th of March, and therefore I issue an order as to the measures to be taken by the commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, is there an official record of the number of people who were killed by land-mines after the date of that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By land-mines? As for my unit, no one lost their life due to a land-mine in my unit because we took special security measures on every road we travelled along. At the corps level, I can't give you a precise number, but more than one -- several dozen men were killed by land-mines. And among the MUP forces, I know that several dozen were killed by the land-mines that were laid on the roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As we can see that you issued warnings and that they were arriving from the direction of Albania, in tab 330, there is a document issued by you which speaks of an attempt to enter the territory from Albania from several directions.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you say: "On the 13th of March, 1999 between 0200 and 0245 hours Siptar terrorist forces tried to enter from several directions onto the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia," and so on. You mentioned the border posts in question, and so on.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This happened on the 13th of March, and it was right next to the lake. As you can see on the other map, right next to the lake a group made an attempt, and after firing, they discarded their equipment and returned to the territory of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So there was a clash and they were driven back. There were no losses.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. There were no losses and they pulled back onto the territory of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what did your order in tab 331 imply, where you speak of maintaining and upgrading combat readiness in the period from the 13th to the 19th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also based on an order from the higher command that combat training was to be intensified of the regular and reserve forces of the brigade according to the existing plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does this refer exclusively to training and exercises?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. By the 15th of March, we were to complete the intake and deployment of soldiers from indirect recruitment. We had received young soldiers who had just completed their training and they were now to be received, issued with weapons. They were to carry out target practice and take part in the necessary number of exercises. The decision was that the -- that the soldiers from the March batch should remain in the units until their status was resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, what is the content of your information on -- of the 14th of March, which is here in tab 332? What is this about actually?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is similar to what happened in the village of Jeskovo. Shall I read paragraph 1? "In the past few days, an STS Staff was set up in the area of Kabas village east of Korisa village." If we can have the map, please. Here's the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's first go back to the end of this document, and then I will ask you about its content. Is this a request by you to the higher command to approve the use of the unit to break up the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of the village of Kabas?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my report to the effect that the terrorist forces were there, that they had arrived in that time period, that they were mobilising the population by force. And in the last part, I ask the command of the corps for approval to neutralise and break up these forces. The village of Korisa, as you can see -- or, rather, the village of Kabas -- the village of Kabas is in the mountains and the Korisa village is near the road. And from there they were threatening the Prizren-Suva Reka-Pristina road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have an estimate here as to the number of Siptar terrorist forces in the area? In point 1, you say that "Around the -- according to information gathered, the STS numbered around 80 men."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, around 40 of them were armed, and it says that part of the Siptar population from Korisa village is moving out in order to avoid forced mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The map we are looking at is tab 337; is it right? I guess so. Could you read the legend there so that we can understand the meaning of it, the red and yellow ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The wider line of the blockade, that's one stage. And the other stage is the stage of the narrower line of the blockade. One is the broader line of the blockade and the other is the narrow line of the blockade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did you get an order from a higher command in connection with this report of yours and your proposals? Is this the order in tab 333?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is an order from the corps command?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I received an order, as in the previous case, to begin preparations and to submit once again my plan for the carrying-out of this task and to say what forces I planned to engage. I was to submit this to the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the order that you received, in point 1 it says -- what does it say?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Prepare, organise, and in cooperation with MUP forces clear the blockade, break up and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the general area of Kabas and Korisa."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And what was the content of your plan in connection with this order, the plan that you submitted to the corps command and which we can find in tab 334? Is this something you sent to the corps command?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is your plan for the breaking-up and destroying of the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Kabas village.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What I say here is what forces will be engaged, from what compositions of the forces. Then it mentions the MUP forces, members of the 37th Detachment and the 5th Company of the special police units. I mention the number of forces and then the plan for the deployment of forces for this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In 335, you have an order issued by General Lazarevic in connection with the same matter in Kabas.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On receipt of my plan, he issued an order that I was to carry it out; in other words, he approved my plan. As of the 15th of March, 1999 I was to begin implementation of the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this is what you indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How were the forces deployed and what happened? There was the broader blockade, the narrow blockade, and the implementation of the plan. On the basis of this, you issued an order on the deployment of forces.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First it contains information on the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this tab 336, this order of yours?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Does it resemble the order you issued in the case of the village of Jeskovo?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's very similar because it follows the rules for the use of units, as provided for by our instructions for the work of the staffs and commands, containing all the elements required.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this whole procedure of issuing an -- making a decision, receiving orders, and so on and so forth, finally led to the implementation of the order and the breaking-up of the Siptar forces in this area.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, tell me now, as this action was underway, I assume that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the implementation of the plan is found in your analysis in tab 338.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is an analysis of the activity to destroy the Siptar forces in the Kabas village sector. Tab 338. Before I ask you about this, I would like you to comment on something else. In paragraph -- or rather, in point 1, in paragraph 2 it says that in Kabas village there were no civilians, only the members of the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Kabas used to be a big village. But as it's in the mountains, the population moved to Korisa. They built houses there, and Korisa was a much larger village. Only about ten houses were left in Kabas and there were no civilians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you say there were hardly ten houses there, you mean inhabited houses?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were houses that were derelict because they'd been abandoned, because the population had moved to Korisa, down to the valley. In the village of Kabas, there was no arable land. It was a mountainous area and the conditions for life were quite difficult there. It didn't even have a good road. It was quite hard to reach.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And what was established -- or rather, what finally happened in this action?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this action, I will just tell you how it ended. We didn't manage to block the terrorist forces on time, so that they pulled out. The larger part of these forces managed to pull out in this direction, towards these other villages and towards the mountain. As it says here, we estimated that the terrorists had 11 killed, no one was captured. On our side, Private Markovic was killed and one soldier was wounded. As for the MUP, I'm not sure what consequences they suffered, but it says here that -- or rather, it says here what was found when we arrived there, referring to their equipment and materiel and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. In tab 339, you have an order that pertains to the organisation of the defence of axes dated the 15th of March, 1999, in order to close off these axes coming from Albania and leading to Metohija, in order to prevent any surprise. What was the reason for this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already in February we were thinking about that, and there were quite a few indicators that NATO would carry out an aggression. In March, it became practically a certainty. As it says here: "According to available operative information, a partial mobilisation of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Albania is underway. That is the second division from Kuks and Bajram Curi. In addition to that, the Siptar forces from 6 to 8.000 have stepped up training in military camps in the north of Albania; Kruma, Vlahna, Zogaj, Vucidol [phoen] and others. In camps in Northern Albania they were being trained by NATO instructors. And it is possible to have engagement of stronger STS forces with stronger NATO air-ground support along the Kuks-Vrbnica-Prizren and the Cafa Pruse-Djakovica axes. Vrbnica-Prizren is this, and further on Suva Reka. That is a road of operative importance; whereas, Cafa Pruse-Djakovica is of tactical importance. In my zone, there were other tactical lines of importance, but through this order I am telling my commanders to take measures in order to close off these axes so that the Siptar terrorist forces or the forces of the Republic of Albania or NATO forces could not penetrate the country along these axes." That is what paragraph 1 speaks of. And paragraph 2 says that "By relying on the present disposition and engagement of forces additional measure should be taken to effectively defend the axes, focussing on setting up obstacles in front of the forward line, gaps," et cetera. And then 3 is "Reinforcing existing forces, and to defend the Vrbnica-Prizren axis, additionally engage an anti-armour missile platoon and six 20/3 millimetre PAT from the PVO to that battalion." And I additionally engage a tank platoon from the armoured battalion and a mechanised platoon from the 243rd Motorised Brigade by the 18th of March. That is for my own forces. As for this mechanised platoon, that would be by the 18th; whereas, my forces by the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that's the activity at that point in time, sealing off the axes where operations could be expected from the territory of the Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task of my brigade was always - and that is why it was in this part of this territory of ours - I mean, it was due to the danger that was imminent from the territory of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You gave an order that has to do with the protection of troops and materiel. That is contained in tab 340. Is it necessary for us to have a special look at it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any kind of non-combat conduct is energetically opposed. And also people should have proper furlough. One-third of the unit should be in the -- on the ready so that conditions can be created for engaging the unit as a whole at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You've been using an expression here in this document. Let me just have a look at this. You use the expression "show of force." Could you please explain that. In the document that is in tab 343, where it says: "Demonstration of force in cooperation with the forces of the MUP on the Prizren-Orahovac axis." General, could you please be so kind as to explain what the purpose of this kind of activity is and what this demonstration of force is that is referred to in this document of yours.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, this is a request that I'm sending to the corps command to "review the overall security situation in the Orahovac municipality area and with the aim of undertaking measures of demonstration of force in order to reassure the Serb people in this area, on the 20th of March, 1993 in the period from 1300 to 1800 hours, together with MUP forces engage in the movement of a part of the forces with a demonstration of force on the Prizren-Zrze-Orahovac axis and come out in the section of the road towards Brestovac village up to the height of the Velika Hoca village."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At that time, was the Serb population moving out and was there a great degree of fear among the Serb population in the area that we're speaking of?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was great fear because similarly, as in 1998, the terrorist forces again did not honour the agreement that was reached when this OSCE mission came; namely, that everybody would remain at the positions where they were. A large section of the territory was placed under their control again, about 40 per cent of it. Again, they placed these local roads under their control as well. A large number of civilians were killed and kidnapped. There's an additional reason too: From the village of Velika Hoca, two brothers were kidnapped. One was killed and the other one was seriously wounded but returned through the mediation of the OSCE. There was this fear among the population and that is why I sought such activity. Also, the terrorists who were close to this road were supposed to see the force that the army had available in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this document in tab 343 you got General Lazarevic's approval to have this movement of troops.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I had proposed. And I was told that if the terrorist forces attack, I should act in accordance with the rules of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, the basic activity that you envisaged was movement.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, movement, and also collecting information during movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in document 345, which is dated the 20th of March, 1999, it says: "In Orahovac we learned that during the day the local Siptar people left --" now, I cannot read this word because it's illegible.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Five to six."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, your version must be more legible: "-- five to six buses for Macedonia."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this approved activity, this came as the report that we were sending to the corps command, reporting on what we noticed during our movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that what you said, that the point of the activity was movement and collecting information?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: About the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And where we were exactly, what we observed. This is information from Orahovac, that part of the Siptar population - probably assessing the situation as being very difficult and believing that there might be an aggression - they wanted to seek shelter and they therefore went to a safe place, to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You wrote a warning about taking safety and security measures, the 21st of March, to the command of group 1/1. Why did you draft this?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this preamble, I'm telling the commanders that the situation is becoming increasingly complex and that Siptar forces can be expected to carry out various acts of provocation, attack individual and small groups of motor vehicles, isolated facilities, barracks, and parts of units in the area. It is possible that incidents may be caused on the border with the Republic of Albania and large sabotage groups may be infiltrated from the territory of the Republic of Albania. Threats of airstrikes are increasingly frequent too. On the basis of all of that, in order to prevent surprise attacks and avoid giving reason for possible airstrikes, I caution that they take special precautionary measures, that is to say, all units in the area along the border, according to available information, preparations are underway for the infiltration of strong STS from the Republic of Albania are underway, as I said, and that they must take full measures to prevent the infiltration of weapons, and that the movement and activities of individuals, small groups and units should be reduced to a minimum in order to avoid acts of provocation by Siptar forces that would provoke a response from our forces which might then be used as a pretext or justification for airstrikes. I ask, therefore, all units to be prepared for a dispersed deployment and that all commanders within their deployment find reserve deployment positions too and to identify possible places for setting up false positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in the documents that follow, are there also warnings -- or, rather, orders improving security along the state border and the possibility of infiltration of larger groups from Albania? I'm referring to 347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what we dealt with is tab 346. Please indicate the tab numbers before you come into the content of it. And for the record, I have to note that the -- Lazarevic's permission is tab 344, not 343, as indicated by the accused. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kwon. I probably made an error regarding the number of the tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In document 347, we see that tensions are on the rise from one day to the other and also the possibility of further infiltrations from Albania.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information was received about a terrorist group of 80 persons, and their objective would be to carry out urban guerilla warfare in the town of Prizren, and that is why all units are being warned to take additional security measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In document 348, then, there is reference to increasingly frequent attacks against members of the army and the MUP, and then a warning is issued as to the kind of measures that should be taken for the sake of protection. Is that the focus of activity at that moment? Defence against possible attacks, is that the focus?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. But there is also a warning being issued because terrorist attacks had already been carried out in Podujevo and Kosovska Mitrovica using explosive devices. Therefore, the command is warning, inter alia, to avoid moving about in uniform in public places, to avoid markets and other public places because these explosive devices had been placed at marketplaces. When vehicles move about, they should be in combat lines, as was defined in earlier orders. And also, before being sent anywhere for -- on assignments outside the zone, that precise information should be provided as to where they would be moving, how they should act in different situations, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Already in the next document - that is to say, number 349 - you say that a large group from Albania would cross the state border.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Information was received that the infiltration of a large group was expected and that in this group there would be members of the Main Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you ordered the sealing-off of all axes and the taking of all relevant positions.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drina 213 and Drina 214 is a code for particular places where there is the possibility of this infiltration.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no translation of 349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And I think this applies to the last two as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that you will be receiving these translations because the documents had been submitted to the appropriate service 70 days ago. As usual, I tender these documents into evidence, Mr. Robinson, and again where there are no translations, could they please be marked for identification for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is -- that's granted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, on the 24th of March, you adopted -- you made an order that has to do with measures for maintaining the combat readiness of the brigade. What does this pertain to?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's already the 24th of March. The military political situation is so serious and there are direct threats of missile attacks by NATO forces and therefore I order the units of my brigade from the 24th of March, 1999, the positions of the sectors of concentration of military hardware units shall be changed daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You do that in order to avoid airstrikes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the main and only reason. They should have camouflage and they should change their positions every day because air surveillance had been carried out throughout this period, our positions were located, and there might be airstrikes against us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about measures to prevent Siptar terrorist forces from being infiltrated from the territory of Albania? Unfortunately, my copy is a very, very poor photocopy, so it's basically useless. I hope yours isn't that bad. Could you just indicate what this is about. I can read that it is an order to prevent the infiltration of Siptar terrorist forces from Albania. You give a map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you talk about the enemy.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the 23rd of March, 1999, and point 1 there is direct reference to the broader situation in our area. Also, it is stated that Albania has carried out a partial mobilisation of its forces, bringing them to Kuks and Bajram Curi, that 6 to 8.000 forces are in camps along the border, and in the zone of the brigade strong forces are engaged along these two axes. And then I say what forces are expected and in which area. From the area of Kuks about 3.000 terrorists are expected, the strength of two brigades. From Kumovlaca [phoen], one brigade, about 1.500 terrorists. And from Zogaj, about 1.000 terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Here in this order when you mentioned the tasks of the 549th Motorised Brigade, how could you describe these tasks, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, very briefly these tasks could be described as tasks to prevent -- or rather, protect the state border and integrity of the state and to prevent forces from the territory of Albania from infiltrating that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have a map, and it says it's a decision of the commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade. It's an order that concerns the prevention of infiltration of Siptar and Albanian forces from the territory of Albania.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that decision, which is also referred to in the map, can you see what the -- the task that you are now referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that's tab 352.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the map is tab 352, and the written text is under tab 351. 352 is the decision referred to in the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map shows the deployment of my four units which were in the border area. Their tasks are also depicted, as well as the terrorist forces in Albania. And there's reference to the tasks of my forces. If infiltration is attempted, they should take this borderline and in cooperation with the security provided for the line at Karaula they were prevent the infiltration of these forces along these axes. The axes of Vrbnica towards Prizren and Dobragorazde [phoen] towards Prizren and then the axis from Cafka [phoen] to Brune [phoen], which leads to Orahovac, and then the axis from Cafa Pruse, the border crossing in the direction of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, since Mr. Nice continues to claim that our army was involved in killing civilians and expelling civilians, and given the tasks that you had that were assigned to the brigade in your order, given the specific activities they were involved in, well, were these the tasks that you had or were there any other hidden tasks that you had? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, there were no other tasks. The army just had the professional task of protecting its state border and no other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You received an order to take measures on the 24th of March. That was when the NATO aggression commenced. What does your order contain? Under tab 353 you issued an order on that date. And it says: "Threats of -- that NATO will bombard the FRY and I hereby order," and then the order follows. What does your order contain?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an order that I issued to commanders. And since we had realised that the airstrike was just a matter of hours - it was no longer even a matter of days - we said that in case our country, any part of our country was bombed, the units should adopt the planned positions. Before this period, the units were in the barracks and only these parts of units were in positions along the border. That was in the border belt. So each and every unit had a plan for engagement which was drawn up on the basis of its main task. And my main task was always to prevent infiltration from the territory of Albania. Therefore, in the case of aggression against our country, my units should move from the barracks and go to the sectors assigned to them near the border and they were to prepare to defend the state territory. And under item 2, it says as soon as the NATO air forces approach the border, they should be attacked. The air should be secured in relation to the possibility of manoeuvring for helicopters and other aircraft. If communications were interrupted -- if the NATO commenced airstrikes and if communications were interrupted, the forces were to be engaged in spite of the fact that communications with the corps could be interrupted, they were to engage in accordance with the previously issued orders. And if an airstrike had already been carried out, there was information on how to deal with the consequences. And when dealing with the consequences, priority was to be given to taking care of the wounded and preventing the spreading of panic, to preventing cases of desertion, in cases of crimes being committed, presenting -- preventing individuals from acting recklessly in the units, preventing sabotage actions against units, detecting the acts of agents and preventing them, informing the superior command or the closest command about the strike and the consequences, and reconnaissance was also to be carried out in the sectors where strikes had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We have a map that is a plan for the defence operation of the Pristina Corps. Could you please have a look at that map too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I stand up to explain this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a plan for the defence operation for the Pristina Corps. This is an excerpt that I was provided for my brigade. The map is a far larger one, and you can see the deployment of all the units in that map. All I have is this excerpt, this part of the map, and this map shows the sort of tasks that my unit had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the entire map is a defence plan for the Pristina Corps, which covered the entire area of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they covered the entire area of Kosovo and Metohija. As a commander, this was sufficient for me because this is where my zone of activity was, this is where my units were deployed. And I can also see where the neighbouring units were deployed. Whereas, the other adjacent units in the depth weren't even important. Here reference is made to the NATO forces, to their strength and where they were grouped, and it was said that the main NATO forces were to carry out an attack from Macedonia towards Kacanik, Uris [phoen], and Pristina and it was said that secondary forces were to launch an attack on my axis. And this order shows that I -- or rather, my brigade were in the first combat echelon of the corps. But on the secondary axis -- I was defending two axes. The operative axis, Vrbnica-Prizren-Suva Reka-Pristina and the tactical axis, Djakovica -- or rather, from the Prusit pass to Djakovica, Klina and Pristina. Here we can see the sort of reinforcements available, how my brigade was reinforced from other units. Tasks were issued to all units and the amount of ammunition allocated for this operation is also referred to, as well as other materiel and technical equipment. And on the basis of this plan, in addition to the basic positions, there are other positions, positions in the depth, right up to the Milanovac Mountain. The objective of the action of the corps forces was that the units in the first echelon - in this case, my brigade - should engage the enemy strike, and then by mounting a defence from the first and second position and from other positions, we were to break the enemy's force, stop the enemy attack, and continue to the second echelon of the corps, which is from the Dulje pass to the Milanovac Mountain and continues in the direction of Orahovac -- or rather, the Dela peak. That would be the axis. Along that axis, the attack was to be stopped. The NATO force and Siptar attack was to be stopped. And we were to completely destroy the enemy's capability of launching attack and launch a counterattack in order to drive enemy forces out of our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in 355 there is a map -- under tab 355, there is a map which is a defence map for the 549th Brigade. Does that relate to the map for the entire corps, and could you briefly say what the defence plan for the country was?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This map, which was drawn up by my brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, if it's a convenient time, we could take the break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I have already put my question to you -- I put a question to you and then we were interrupted by the break. You were explaining the map for the defence of the Pristina Corps, and now we have in front of us a map with the plan for the 449th Brigade [as interpreted] defence. That's your brigade. Tell us, what sort of a plan did they have?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, in the plan for the defence operation of the Pristina Corps, we could see the deployment of my units. In this map, we also have the deployment but also for lower units, units two levels below. So you also have company positions depicted here. The plan was as follows: First of all, there's information on the enemy provided here in the zone of defence of my brigade, and if you look at the border towards Albania and then to Macedonia and to the peak of Plesko [phoen], it's about 150 kilometres long. We were expecting the aggressor forces and terrorist forces to come from two directions, Albania and Macedonia, from the Tetovo direction. Here there's reference to the purpose of those forces, the objective of those forces. And as it says here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, General. What is the purpose of this evidence? Is there -- is there any charge in the indictment to which is it relevant, any incident in the indictment to which this kind of evidence is relevant?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, such evidence is relevant for all the charges in the case. Mr. Robinson, I would like to remind you of the fact that Mr. Nice has a certain position that the -- that the FRY and Serbian forces were to encircle inhabited places, they would shell them, enter those places, separate the men and women, kill the men, drive them away to Albania, et cetera. And now you're being presented with a totally different picture with regard to how the army conducted itself on a daily basis. There's analysis provided for each and every movement of the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this picture does not contradict that. You're telling us about how well-organised, how well-trained, how orderly the VJ forces are. That doesn't in any way, in my view, rebut the -- the allegations in the indictment. You have to deal with specific -- the specific incidents in the indictment. I mean, merely to show that the VJ was well-trained, well-organised, had plans which required them to follow the rules of combat, which required them to follow the Geneva Conventions. All of that by itself is not -- is not relevant. If it is relevant, it's only marginally relevant. You have to deal with the -- with the incidents. And I have to ask myself whether this is a proper use of the Court's time. I'll consult my colleagues on this -- on this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before you consult your colleagues, let me draw your attention to the essence of the matter. The thing is not only to show whether the army was well trained, well disciplined, respected the Geneva Conventions, and so on and so forth, but every document shows the precise tasks that the army had and how it carried them out. From looking at these tasks, you can see that the army was exclusively on the defensive. It was not engaged in expelling the population, killing civilians, or anything like that. You can see that what General Delic is saying completely invalidates the testimony of particular witnesses, and he's speaking of events in which he himself participated and in which his units participated. So these are the tasks, not just on paper but the tasks that the army carried out, and we're getting evidence as to how they were carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You made one point that is worth considering. You say that these plans show that the army was on the defensive. Let's consider that. How -- how do they show that? If they show that, I think that's relevant. How do they show that the army was always on the defensive?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The general will explain. He will explain what their task was. You saw in the order that we have just dealt with that it was a question of defence, the deployment of units for defence. When speaking of the enemy, reference is made to NATO and to the Siptar sabotage forces. There is not a single task either assigned to the army or carried out by the army that had anything to do with destroying villages, persecuting civilians, or anything similar to that. This was a large section of the army commanded by General Delic which is representative of the behaviour of the army as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, can you assist us on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see from the tabs at 353 onwards that we are getting into pertinent dates, 24th of March, 1999, and plans for defence in relation to proposed NATO bombing. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. If you move further through these tabs, 356 onwards, you'll see at 356 that you have places such as Suva Reka mentioned, Velika Krusa, Donje Retimlje, all places that have been relevant to the indictment. 357 is Suva Reka. Coming up further, we've got Celine at 369, which, of course, I think the first crime base dealt with, Vehi Melsani [phoen], I think that was Celine. And we've also got Bela Crkva at 366, 365, 363 as well. So I think we're coming into areas of explanation from the witness in relation to quite pertinent matters in the indictment. This is from the file that we've just been disclosed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Kay. Thanks. Well, Mr. Milosevic, let the witness concentrate on showing that the plans were defensive.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you heard. Explain the map in the briefest possible way and then we will move on.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map itself, as the title says, is a plan of defensive combat. An aggression was expected on my units from the territories of Albania and Macedonia. The goal of the enemy activity in the first echelon, in the first stage, was to take the Djakovica-Prizren line. In the second stage, to take the Orahovac-Suva Reka line, where they would introduce a second echelon for the purpose of carrying out further combat activities in the direction of Prizren. As for the defence, there were two stages: The first stage, lasting seven to eight days, was to be carried out by my brigade. During seven or eight days my brigade was from these successive positions - these are the basic positions and the yellow ones are reserve positions and the ones with dots are the next positions in depth - so during seven or eight days they were to break the enemy force's advances from Albania and the forces advancing towards Prizren, and in the second echelon of the Pristina Corps from the line Milanovac-Dulje-Jezerska Planeja [phoen] - Nazar Planeja they were to halt the incursion of the enemy from the direction of Albania and mount a counter-attack to drive these forces from the territory of our country. In order to carry out this task, my unit was reinforced with several other units from the Pristina Corps. First of all, it was reinforced with the 354th Detachment from the 354th Brigade. The 68th territorial detachment, the 108th military territorial detachment, one battery of 122-millimetre multiple rocket launchers, the border battalions, the 55th Border Battalion and a company from the 53rd Border Battalion were also resubordinated under my command, as well as several other lower-ranking units. Apart from this, the plan envisaged the mining of the entire state border toward the Republic of Albania, and these were to be both anti-tank and anti-personnel mines. It was expected that up to 35 bomber planes were to be used against my unit, up to 50 GO rocket attacks, and 91 helicopter squadrons and other helicopters, general-purpose helicopters. In this plan, we see that the use of short-term chemical weapons was expected as well as depleted uranium weapons. As we can see from this map, my decision was to group my forces as follows: In the first combat echelon, there were to be two battalions. On the axis towards Albania and on the axis towards Macedonia, the 68th Detachment. There was to be one motorised battalion here, and on this axis from the Republic of Macedonia, the remaining forces of the military territorial Prizren detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, thanks very much. You were preparing for an assault from land.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a ground attack and airstrikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic. I think we have the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Before we proceed further, General, I will quote from this document 353 that we've already dealt with. And in point 1.5 of your order, you say prevent the joining-up of the Siptar forces with NATO, and in 4 you say prevent sabotage activities against the unit. From this, can we see that your defensive operations also implied firing on the Siptar terrorist forces which were still in the depth of the territory in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was obvious - and we've spoken of this before - was that along with an attack from the territory of Albania and an attack from Macedonia, on the Prizren-Djakovica access there was a territory under the control of the Siptar terrorist forces, and the expectation was that when the airstrikes began, these forces which were in the depth of the territory would set out to cut off the communications and to strike in the rear of our units in order to cooperate with the forces attacking from the Republics of Albania and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. I hope that's clear to everybody. Now let us move on to deal with specific places, the specific places in the allegations made by Mr. Nice and which are located in your area of responsibility. We shall begin with Orahovac municipality. Is there is a document entitled "Order: To provide support to the MUP forces in breaking up and destroying the Siptar forces in Orahovac, Suva Reka and Velika Krusa." This is at tab 356. Have you found it, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does this refer to what you have just spoken of, their cooperation with the NATO aggressors and the expected attacks from the territories of Albania and Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This refers to the terrorist forces -- or rather, the two brigades that were in my area of responsibility. One of these brigades was here in the Retimlje area and the other in the Drenovac area. Also, there were local terrorist staffs in Velika Krusa, Brestovac, Donje Retimlje, and so on. It also mentions what weapons they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This document is very clear, well laid out, so let's not dwell on it any longer. Will you please now look at number 357. The title is "Order on destroying Siptar terrorist forces in the general sector of the village of Retimlje, lifting the blockade of the Suva Reka-Orahovac road and establishing control of the territory." What does this document contain?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document was issued by the Pristina Corps. This second document is my own order for the implementation of the task ordered by the corps. In the information about the enemy, more details are provided. The Siptar forces have reorganised, equipped themselves with modern weapons and trained to continue their arms struggle against the defence forces of the FRY. The strongest STS strongholds in the general areas of Retimlje, Milanovac, the village of Studencani, the village of Samodraze, the village of Dobrodeljane and Pagarusa. In this zone, the Podenje-Pastrik [phoen] operations zone, there were two brigades of the KLA, one in the village of Velika Drenovac [phoen], the other in the village of Retimlje. The commander -- command post is in Morilja [phoen] and the local staffs are in other villages. There is mention of the fact that in each of these villages there are armed local guards consisting of 30 to 50 terrorists. The aim of the terrorists was to take over military, commercial, and public facilities, expand and consolidate operation zones, broaden the scope of armed rebellion, and create conditions for taking control of Kosovo and Metohija as well as to declare an independent Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, as this is a very detailed order, I won't go into it in detail. Everyone can read it. But let me draw your attention to page 4, to point 8.2 in which, among other things, it says the following: "Escort captured terrorists to the POW concentration point to the administrative building of Metohija Vino in the settlement of Siroka [phoen] near Suva Reka and the wine cellars in Mala Krusa." And then you go on to say: "In the course of combat operations, I exclusively forbid unsupervised ventures into populated localities, plunder of property of the local population, violations of provisions of international humanitarian law, and relocation of enemy weapons, military equipment or corps, as well as any entry into enemy shelters before the arrival of expert organs." Well, this sentence here, this phrase, "before the arrival of expert organs," refers to teams who should deal with mines and booby-traps. But what it says here about taking captured enemy soldiers to prisoner of war points, is this part of your tender? Have I quoted it correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That was a leading question. I don't have at the moment any view on whether it's significant or not. I'm just looking at this part of this document for the first time. But it's not for the accused to give an explanation for what expert organs are in case there's something significant in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Avoid the leading questions and the comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, my question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in my tab.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, Judge Kwon was speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, what did you say this -- was this order based upon? Was there an order from the upper level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the previous tab.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In tab 356, it says: "Joint command for Kosovo and Metohija." Could you explain that, what does -- what that does mean.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regardless of the fact that it says "joint command," I received this order by post in the same way as I received other orders. And it contained attachments from other organs which said they were from the Pristina Corps, and the number also is from the Pristina Corps, but it's true that it says here "joint command for Kosovo and Metohija." As a brigade commander, I didn't pay attention to this because when I received such orders, I always had a preparatory order from the commander, which arrived by telephone, telling me to prepare the unit and telling me I would get a written order. That's why at the time I didn't attach any significance to this. My explanation of why it says "joint command" is the following: In the course of 1998, when together with members of the MUP we carried out activities against the terrorists in those five stages that I have already explained, at the beginning of each stage we were invited to come to Pristina. We were summoned there, both the army commanders and the police commanders, with our superior officers. And there on the spot coordination was carried out between the police and the army, and we, as the members of the army, and they were handed the documents on the spot. On the ground, we had the necessary documents that enabled us to coordinate our activities. On this occasion, I did not go to Pristina. Neither did my colleague from the Secretariat of the Interior in Prizren. My understanding of why it says "joint command" here is that were it to say "command of the Pristina Corps," then this would not be binding on the MUP. It might be binding only for me. But the two of us were supposed to carry out coordination on the ground. We were supposed to coordinate our activities on the ground, that is. And this joint command I understood as a coordinating body between the army and the MUP and the other state organs in Pristina. This was acceptable both to me and to the MUP. That's my explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was there any legal or practical basis to establish this kind of joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as the fight against terrorism is concerned, the state can use different mechanisms and organise all its resources, after all. This does not have to do with direct combat only or operations by the military and the police. Other institutions as well have to take part in those other forms that we call non-military forms for resolving a crisis. That is why I believe that there had to be coordination, say, at the level of Pristina or the level of the entire province, where there would be people from Belgrade who would directly, on the spot, see what the security and political situation was and where members of the military would be in order to realise part of these measures. I believe that not a single crisis can be resolved if other measures are not included as well; in schooling, health care, with regard to humanitarian and all other issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who headed this joint command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, you're asking me that and I really don't know. I actually never saw this joint command. I never attended a single meeting. I only came across individual persons, if I can put it that way, and I had heard of some persons being in Pristina. At any rate, I was supposed to be in Prizren, and I could go to Pristina only when told to do so by the command. I know that in this coordination body Mr. Minic was there for a while, and Mr. Sainovic, and then I think Mr. Matkovic, as far as the civilian authorities are concerned. I don't know whether it was Mr. Andjelkovic too. As for the MUP, now, was it Mr. Djordjevic? As far as the army was concerned, it was probably the corps commander. But had this been a command that had a commander, then somebody's signature would have been included here. I think that although it was called a command, in my opinion it was a most unfortunate name that was chosen. But anyway, it was a coordination body, a coordinating body. I don't understand why it's really called joint command. It was a coordination body that coordinated the activities of state entities in Kosovo and Metohija. I know that I received several such orders, but I never saw that somebody had signed this. Again, it says "joint command" and there's no signature, but I carried out this order because from my superior officer I had previously received an order to prepare for activity and that I would get my orders in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for your detailed answer. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But why do you say it's an unfortunate name, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, this name also makes you think of commanding. In the Pristina Corps, in my brigade, in the army in general knows "command" according to the chain of command as a rule, from the squad up to the brigade, corps, army, all the way up to the Chief of General Staff. There is a single chain of command. It is well known that in my brigade I was the only one who could issue orders. My Chief of Staff also, who had authority vested in him by me. As for other officers, they could only act within their own line of work and on my approval. I mention these people now, but I could give orders only -- I could, rather, receive orders only from General Lazarevic or his deputy. There was no third person in the corps that could issue an order to me and have me carry that order out. So that's what the rules of conduct envisaged, that the commander of the army can issue an order too, or his Chief of Staff, because that is also involved in the chain of command. So if I'm called directly and issued an order. In practice, this never happened, but the rules envisage that commands can be issued in this way. Also, the rules say that if somebody is skipping over a particular ring in the chain of command, if the commander of the army calls me directly, I'm duty-bound to carry out his order, but it is also my duty to inform my superior officer, that is to say, the corps commander of the order that I received and carried out. That is how the chain of command operates in the army. Of course, I would never accept to carry out an order issued by a civilian, because that is totally unacceptable. And that would totally infringe upon military organisation as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What I find strange in that connection is that -- that so far we don't -- we don't appear to have seen the military order that goes with this. Where is it? You said that you weren't acting on this; you were acting on a military order. So where is the military order? This can easily be clarified and cleared up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, I think you didn't understand. You see, in the same envelope along with this order -- I mean, this is one order. Then I received in the same envelope an order for the engineering operations and also an order for artillery, but "joint command" was not written in the heading. It said "command of the Pristina Corps," as usual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That means we'll be coming to -- they must be later in the exhibits then somewhere, are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. These documents do exist. Perhaps they were not considered relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since there is a great deal of interest here in this expression "joint command," tell me, General, did you ever receive or carry out any order that had not come from your own superior command, the command of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's what I've already explained. It's not only that I didn't carry it out; I'd never carry out an order that did not come from persons who had the right to issue orders to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you show a few minutes ago the order of the Pristina Corps on the map of the Pristina Corps and did you show your own order on the map of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are these orders that include the operations pertaining to support for crushing the anti- -- the terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This has to do with a specific order for a specific area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But within something that is already covered in the orders that you quoted a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From the point of view of territory and command.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan that got in from the Pristina Corps fully covered this activity as well and all other activities that would evolve later in this territory, because the deployment in this plan would not change until combat operations stopped after the agreement. The deployment of my units would remain as depicted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, which -- which tab is that order in, the one that you're referring to? It's obviously a tab we've dealt with already. Which one is it? Can you remind me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's a plan, the plan for the defence operation of the Pristina Corps, what Mr. Milosevic asked me about, and the plan for defence of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Look, please, at 351. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an order of mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the 20th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, Mr. -- Mr. Milosevic's leading questions don't help me to identify -- he's now saying there is a document that we've already seen which is the order from -- a military order that you were working on and all that we were looking on -- looking at from the Supreme Command was something that we had already seen you were ordered to do by an appropriate military document. Now, I would like to see that document. And if it's not here, then we shouldn't be misled in that way. So let's have the position clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. General, have we seen this? Have you explained on the map the defence plan of the Pristina Corps for all of Kosovo and Metohija and then the defence plan of your own brigade, which now moves, as you said, in greater detail than the plan of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is actually a subtle form of leading to try and get round the difficulty that's been identified by the question from the Bench. The accused --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I doubt if it matters. I was about to ask: Is the document -- is the plan something that was sent from a higher military commander to the general? Because if it's not, then it's not the document we're looking for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already shown it. It's under this map, the text of the map -- of the plan and the map of the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. But is -- is the plan a document that was sent to you by someone else, or is the plan something you yourself prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part -- or rather, this map -- this plan is what I compiled myself on the basis of the document that I received from the Pristina Corps, from my superior command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm looking for the one that you got from the Pristina Corps, from your superior command. That's what I'm -- that's what I'd like to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Mr. Delic, if you could take a look at tab 321 or 323. It's an order -- a telegram from the Pristina command -- corps command. It's before the war. And the Pristina Corps' command, using that term, and the serial -- confidential number is 455 -- 455-20 and -21.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just give me the tab?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, 2 -- I'm sorry, 321 or 323.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, this has something to do with a completely different operation that we explained and we presented all the documents of the corps and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There Pristina Corps' command are using the term "Pristina Corps command" as they stand. But now 356 they are using a different name, "joint command for Kosovo and Metohija," while using the same serial number starting with 455. So it -- what you are saying is that this is the -- exactly the order from the Pristina Corps? Or you received a separate order from the Pristina Corps other than this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There was no other order apart from the one that says "joint command" in the heading. I already said that in the same envelope I received something else too. I tried to explain that to you a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just go back to the map that contains the order of the Pristina Corps to defend Kosovo and Metohija, the one that you received in part. What is the name of that order and what is the name of that map that has to do with the entire Pristina Corps? Then you had your own map that has to do with your own brigade only and that is that you formulated through your order.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map of the Pristina Corps is the plan of the defence operation of the Pristina Corps. It's right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Take out the first one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is presented through the text and through the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that the order of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it signed by the commander of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got only an excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But an excerpt from the order of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note they cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this from the order of the commander of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of which I made my own plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you should stop -- stop for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's tab 354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you speak of the -- the order of the Pristina Corps, what order is that? The witness can answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the plan, the plan for a defence operation. I said that it has text of its own and a schematic breakdown which is quite clear, and you have items relating to orders for a defence operation. You have an overview of the units that will be engaged and the axis on which they will be engaged. Reference is also made to the stages involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, is the map we are now looking at an excerpt or part of the map which follows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map that follows was drawn on the basis of this map. This is what I received from the corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who was the map -- which contains the entire Kosovo, the fuller one, the bigger one? It's a different one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The larger map shows all the brigades in Kosovo and Metohija. But as a brigade commander, the corps didn't send everything to me, they sent me this part that was of interest to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was the larger map drawn by the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the larger perhaps was drawn by the Pristina Corps, but they only sent me this part, which was of interest to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So do -- can we see the signature in the larger map of the commander of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means. But I don't have that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm looking -- I'm referring to tab 355, the one which follows that map, the bigger map, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the larger map is mine. It's signed by the commander who authorised my map, and it has my signature too. It bears my signature. So this map was drawn up on the basis of the -- my map. I sent that map for -- to be approved by the corps command. The corps command approved my decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I just want to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Judge Kwon and Judge Bonomy have questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, on the map that's now on the -- the board, which is 354, does it say "Pristina Corps" on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, it's not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the map was sent in an envelope with documents attached to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it signed by anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand why you fail to understand this. The map that this map is based on was signed by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But this particular one you say is the one you received.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
