utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this, as I have said, is just a part of the map, and it's for my brigade. It's based on the large map that the corps had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. But that is the one that was sent to you because it related to the area which was within your area -- it related to your area of responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So does it have the words "Pristina Corps" on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says: "A plan for defence operation for Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does it say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you show me where it says that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the top. And is it signed by anyone? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How is it that you don't understand that this map is just a photocopy of part of a map that the Pristina Corps had. My map, which is based on this map, was signed by the corps commander. This map -- well, we have to have two copies of this map: One is kept in the corps and another is kept in the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How do you know that the original of this was signed by the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, how do I know that the corps commander signed it? Well, the corps commander drew the map and signed it. That's common practice. That's quite usual. You can see how he signed my map. Why did he do that? Well, because that is the procedure that is followed in the army. I sign a map that I draw and the corps commander signs to show that he is approving my plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you -- you obviously think it's -- it's very strange for me to wonder why the document that you say is actually sent to you from your command on the basis of which you are to act should be signed. It's just very foolish of me to think that that document -- one might expect that document to be signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was certainly signed, the document in the Pristina Corps. This is part of the main map that was sent to me. The commander signed the map that was kept in the corps, and this is what he sent to me. There was no need to sign every part of that map, every excerpt from that map. We can have a look at other documents. We can see other documents for which there was a main map and then there was an excerpt that concerned the 449th Brigade [as interpreted]; that is to say, that only concerned my brigade. So the part of the map that was relevant to me was taken. You can see that this map continues in all directions. The commander provided me with what I needed, provided me with information about his decision with regard to my zone and provided me with information on the adjacent units. That's what I had to know. And my map is completely identical to this map, because I can't change the positions that were allocated to me by my superior. And this map was sent to the corps command for approval, and I signed it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, there is some confusion here, a misunderstanding, because Mr. Bonomy asked you whether you were surprised by the fact that he said that he expected the map to be signed. If a command issues a map, is it always signed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as you can see here, my map was signed by General Lazarevic, so it had been sent for approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, on the basis of this part of the map that relates to the entire Pristina Corps, in that part of the map, does it say "Plan for a defence operation for the Pristina Corps"?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of that excerpt which concerns your brigade, did you draw a map which says "Defence plan for the 549 Brigade"?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And does it have to fully relay the order of the higher command and then do you have to provide an analysis of it for two levels below?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And when you draw such a map, on the basis of an excerpt from the higher command, does it have to be sent to the superior command for approval?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, and it's been signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And General Lazarevic, the commander of the Pristina Corps, signed a map that was based on his map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And could he have signed a map that wasn't based on his map?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he checked this and compared what I had done with what he had on his map, well, he certainly wouldn't have signed it if there had been any differences, even minor differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are there any differences between your map and the excerpt of the corps map apart from the fact that the level of detail is different?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only the detail is different but nothing else is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So as far as the details are concerned, what are the differences? In your map, you also show lower units that aren't referred to in the corps map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps map depicts the position of battalions, and I also have to depict the position of companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So within the framework of a corps map -- with regard to the corps map, you only depicted the position of companies.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, the battalions were depicted in accordance with the corps plan and we depicted the position of companies. Those are the details concerned. And naturally, the scale of my map was different. The scale of the map for the corps was 1 to 200.000 and my scale was 1 to 50.000. And that's because the corps has to depict the position of all the units and I only have to show my zone of responsibility and the position of my units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think we have managed to clarify this. Can we finally go back to the document under tab 357, which says: "Order on destroying the STS in the general sector of the village of Retimlje, lifting the blockade of the Suva Reka-Orahovac road and establishing control of the territory." This is a document that appears under tab 357. General, is that a document of yours?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is an order that I drafted on the basis of an order from the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since this concerns the Retimlje sector and the Suva Reka-Orahovac road and the scale of the map is 1 to 50.000, what information do you have in relation to this? And we referred to your main tasks. What sort of information do you provide here as far as the enemy is concerned?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I could show you the map that accompanies this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that the map that accompanies the order is under tab 358.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before -- just before you move on, you say that you drafted this document, this order on the basis of an order from the Pristina Corps command. Now, have we actually seen that order, or are you referring again to the map that we've seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here it is. It's under tab 356. That's the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That doesn't come from the Pristina Corps command. So we're back to where we started; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, the general is trying to explain this to you. This is an order from the Pristina Corps and the fact that it says "joint command" here is of no significance in his opinion. He received this order from the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... beyond my comprehension at the moment, but no doubt all will become clear in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope so too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, as you have said, there is a map that accompanies this. I wanted you to comment on your order which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Milosevic. Mr. Delic, are you following? The extension seems to be disconnected. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, since you suggested that we should first have a look at the map and then we can go back to the order, what does it say here? What is the title of the map under 358, tab 358? Could you please read out the title.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decision of the commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade to destroy the STS forces in the Orahovac-Suva Reka-Velika Krusa sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What does it say in the upper left-hand corner? Could you read it out, please.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, it says: "I authorise Commander General Major -- Major General Vladimir Lazarevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that the commander of your corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Is that in accordance with the rules of service? You issued an order, you attached a map which was approved of by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whatever I do, whatever my commanders do, has to be approved at a superior level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, tell me, throughout that period of time, did you ever see a single map on the position of your forces, on your operations, that wasn't drawn up by the Pristina Corps command but that was drawn by someone else?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Pristina Corps drew maps for all of its units, and only the Pristina Corps did that, and that was what I did for my units too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, be so kind as to explain this decision. Here you say it's an order that was issued -- well, I'd first like to clarify something of general interest. Is an order at this level always issued in written form and in the form of a map?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's always the case, because naturally an order contains far more information. But when you have a map, it's a lot easier to understand the nature of the commander's decision. That's why it's called the commander's decision. It's sufficient to cast a glance at the map to see what the commander's idea was with regard to carrying out a certain operation or task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So if I put this simply, would the map be a graphic depiction of an order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because on the basis of such a map, a professional, an officer, could draft an order. Perhaps not such a detailed one as this one here, but if it had arrived from some other army -- if they had such a map, they could reconstruct the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They could reconstruct the order with the positions of all the units, their axes of action, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see all of this on the map?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This decision, the commander's decision on destroying the STS forces in such-and-such a sector - I won't mention the sector - well, this is in fact your order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it was approved of, as it says in the upper left-hand corner -- it was approved of by the corps commander, who was your superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So please explain the following for me -- explain this for me.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He ordered this and approved it, and I received the order. There was nothing else for me to do. I issued an order to allocate tasks to my units. And here reference is made to the position of the terrorist forces. And you can see that the terrorist forces were at the north-east of the Prizren-Djakovica road. And here in the Retimlje sector depicted in blue - blue stands for the enemy forces, the terrorist forces in this particular case - in the Retimlje sector, the commander of the -- the command of the 124th Brigade was located and that entire brigade was deployed in this sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you have taken this as an example. You have now read this out from the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That in the Retimlje area that's where the headquarters of the 124th Brigade is located. If we go back to document 357, the text of the order, what it says here is, some ten lines from the beginning: "The 124th KLA Brigade (about 300 terrorists KM) in the village of Retimlje." What you read out from the map differs from the order only in that the order says that there were about 300 terrorists. The other information is also contained in the map. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Before that, it says: "122nd KLA Brigade, about 250 terrorists, command post of Velika Drenovac."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the other side of Orahovac, in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please continue your explanation of the map.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On receipt of the order from the command of the Pristina Corps that the terrorist forces were to be broken up and that control is to be re-established over the territory between Suva Reka, Orahovac, Zrze and Prizren in the immediate rear of the area of deployment of my brigade, I issued a decision to engage part of the forces from this area here on the communication between Prizren and Djakovica to establish a blockade there, to establish another line of blockade in the direction of Suva Reka, and to go with my main forces from the directions of Suva Reka and Orahovac and to break through this territory held by the terrorists, to link up the forces from these two directions, and then to mount a joint attack with the forces from this axis here, Bela Crkva-Hoca and so on in the Retimlje area, and there to break up the terrorist forces, disarm them, and neutralise this territory again and bring it back under the control of the army and the MUP. In other words, to remove the threat to my unit, because at the same time as an attack is mounted from across the border, these units might attack my units from the rear and cut off their communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. This was the plan. These were your orders. This is what you drew on the map. I assume you also implemented it. Did you implement this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were certain problems. Here the Siptar terrorist forces defended themselves persistently. And on the 27th of March, we did not manage to link up our forces from these two axes. It was only in the early morning of the 27th of March that these forces linked up, and it was only then that we can say that we surrounded part of the forces. What was not good in these activities was that in those three days, the 25th, the 26th, and part of the 27th, the main part of the terrorist forces pulled out in the direction of Dobrodelje village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, please, in document 359, is there an analysis of the activities of your brigade in connection with the task you are now explaining?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me read out the first sentence to you. It says here - and you sent this to the command of the Pristina Corps, your superior command - "From the 25th to the 29th --" I'm reading out -- "pursuant to the order to provide support to the MUP forces and the command of the Pristina Corps," strictly confidential number, and so on, you mentioned the numbers: "The Siptar terrorist forces were broken up in the Retimlje area," and so on and so forth. Does it say here quite clearly that this was an order issued by you pursuant to an order from the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this will be the last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a command from the Pristina Corps, number 455-63. If you go back to tab 356, is this order strictly confidential number 455-63?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the order which says "joint command" in the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you say that you received a number from -- an order from the Pristina Corps. You mentioned the same number.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me, sometimes I didn't even notice that it said "joint command."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you received orders from the corps. You reported to the corps. Very well. Thank you, General. We will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn for today, resume tomorrow at 9.00. Before we adjourn, Mr. Milosevic, you made a request yesterday for a videotape of the proceedings. The Chamber has considered this. The Chamber requires that you make a written motion setting out precisely what you wish, whether it is particular passages from the -- from the evidence or whether it is the -- the entire --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entire videotape. It's a very simple request: The entire videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, make a -- make a written motion for it and explain why you need it and the basis for it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I understood that everybody has the right to get a videotape, anyone who is undergoing proceedings here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I've already said what the Chamber has --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Nice, did you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, I was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one question, please. I haven't finished. Mr. Robinson, you recently said -- you just said "tomorrow at 9.00." According to the information I have, you are sitting in the afternoon tomorrow. Has this changed, or have I not been informed on time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are sitting in the morning. And you should have been advised, because originally it was the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, as to the accused's request for a copy of the video, I probably wouldn't wish to be involved in that. But I respectfully draw to your attention one matter of concern: A video of the whole proceedings would, of course, reveal the pictures and images of protected witnesses whereas the transcript in written form, to which the accused is, of course, entitled, does not. That's a matter that the Chamber might want to have in mind as it considers making available to him such a document that would carry permanent images of protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we would certainly have that in mind, Mr. Nice. Yes. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
